headline: Majors hold their 200-day lines while the week runs red and ETF cash walks out the door
paragraphs: Start with the regime, because it's the one clean signal on an otherwise noisy board. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and BNB all sit above their 200-day averages with golden crosses in place, seven-asset agreement minus two: DOGE and ADA sit below their 200-day lines with no golden cross, and both are down over 70% from their 12-month highs versus roughly 38-60% for the majors. That's a split market, five names still in a structural uptrend, two left behind. Bitcoin itself is 38.8% off its $124,739.81 high at $76,352.91, up 0.3% on the day but down 3.5% on the week and up 18.2% on the month, three windows, three different stories, which is exactly why the window matters more than the headline number.

Momentum is the tell that the trend is resting, not accelerating. Every asset in the set shows MACD below signal, including the five names still above their 200-day average. RSI readings cluster in the mid-40s to high-50s (BTC 50.8, ETH 52.1, SOL 51.3, BNB 57.7), which is neutral chop, not overbought and not oversold. Pair that with the week-over-week red across the board (BTC -3.5%, SOL -4.8%, XRP -7.1%, DOGE -10.7%, ADA -11.1%) sitting underneath a green month for all seven, and the picture is a market that ran hard over 30 days and has spent the last week digesting that move without breaking trend structure. Momentum cooling while trend holds is not divergence in the worrying sense, it's a pause.

Positioning adds a wrinkle worth naming plainly. Funding, the periodic payment perpetual-futures longs make to shorts (or vice versa) to keep the contract price tied to spot, is positive and modest across BTC (8.7% annualized), ETH (4.4%) and SOL (4.2%), meaning longs are paying to stay in the trade, a mild but real cost of being bullish with leverage. XRP funding is negative (-0.5%), longs getting paid instead, alongside a long/short account ratio of 3.12, the most lopsided in the set. That combination, mostly-long crowd but shorts getting compensated, plus $1.75M in short liquidations against $212K in longs over six hours, reads as a market where the crowd's directional bet and the derivatives cost of holding it are not lined up. BTC open interest sits at $2.17B, sizable but not flagged as extreme against its own funding rate, so this looks more like ordinary positioning than a crowded, fragile bet.

Flows are where the real tension shows up. Whale wallets moved a net $171.4M off exchanges in the last 24 hours, with BTC contributing $160.9M of that (inflows of $171.8M against outflows of $332.7M) and ETH a smaller $10.5M net off. Zoom out to the weekly series and the direction flips: the week ending Sep 17 shows $593M moving onto exchanges, following $536M onto exchanges the week before that, a two-week run in the opposite direction from today's 24-hour print. That's not a contradiction to paper over, it's two different windows telling two different stories, and both are real. Meanwhile the traditional-finance side is net selling: BTC ETFs saw a $151.8M outflow on 16 Sep 2026 and a $738.2M net outflow over the last five sessions, two consecutive down days. ETH ETFs pulled $94.3M out on the same day but still show a $71.0M net inflow over five sessions, meaning the daily and five-day windows for ETH flows actively disagree. Stablecoin float, the dry powder sitting in USDT and friends, grew a modest 1.1% over 30 days to $309.5B, not a surge, not a drain.

Sentiment closes the loop and mostly just shrugs. The Fear & Greed gauge reads 50, dead neutral, sitting at the low end of its own 30-day range of 46 to 74. That's a crowd that has cooled off from recent greed without tipping into fear, which lines up reasonably well with the cooling MACD readings and the red weekly candles. No sharp disagreement between gauge and tape today, which is itself worth noting since it's the exception rather than the rule.

What to watch from here: whether BTC and ETH ETF flows turn same-direction for more than two sessions in a row (right now BTC has two down days, ETH's daily and five-day numbers still disagree), whether the weekly whale flow flips back to off-exchange after two straight weeks of onto-exchange movement, and whether XRP's negative funding alongside its 3.12 long/short ratio resolves into either a funding flip positive or a fresh round of long-side liquidations. Any of those would mark a change in what's currently a resting, not accelerating, market.
